root_cause.text: The error path in reset_add_gpio_aux_device() calls both auxiliary_device_uninit() and kfree() on the same allocation, but auxiliary_device_uninit() triggers the device release callback reset_gpio_aux_device_release() which already frees the device, resulting in a double free.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the kfree(adev) call after auxiliary_device_uninit(adev) in the __auxiliary_device_add() failure path. The commit message explicitly states that "The device release callback reset_gpio_aux_device_release() frees adev, but the current error path then calls kfree(adev) again, causing a double free." The fix keeps kfree(adev) only for the auxiliary_device_init() failure path (which doesn't trigger the release callback) while removing it after auxiliary_device_uninit() (which does trigger the callback).

bic_trace_step.reason: The function reset_add_gpio_aux_device() contains the vulnerable double-free pattern. At lines 883-886, when __auxiliary_device_add() fails, the code calls both auxiliary_device_uninit(adev) and kfree(adev). The reset_gpio_aux_device_release() callback (lines 855-859) is set as the device release function and will be triggered by auxiliary_device_uninit(), which calls kfree(adev) at line 858. This results in a double free of the same allocation. The fix would require removing the kfree(adev) call after auxiliary_device_uninit(), as the device release callback already handles the memory deallocation.
